summary: Completed the first full Vale S.A. sponsored-ADR review using current SEC-filed second-quarter production, results and IFRS evidence. The deterministic assessment is Hold / Watch and allocation-ineligible: at the USD 13.80 mark, bear/base/bull fair values are USD 9.00/USD 14.50/USD 20.00, probability-weighted expected return is 1.09%, and confidence-adjusted expected return is 0.82%. The 13 August lower-Bollinger-band breach is a timing risk rather than a supported fundamental buy signal. No strategy, signal, order, allocation, execution, cash, portfolio, fill or performance state changed.

evidence.claim: Vale reported second-quarter pro forma EBITDA of US$4.066 billion, free cash flow of US$1.505 billion and net debt of US$13.173 billion; sales increased year over year across iron ore, copper and nickel.
Vale's interim IFRS filing reports first-half 2026 net income attributable to shareholders of US$3.268 billion and diluted earnings per share of US$0.77.
Vale's current production report supports improved year-over-year production and sales across its business segments and supplies the operating evidence required by the cyclical-commodity template.

Deterministic scenario calculation classified Vale Hold / Watch and ineligible, with 5.07% base return, 1.09% expected return, 0.82% confidence-adjusted expected return, 4.83% margin of safety, and failed expected-return, payoff and relationship gates.
The canonical 13 August 2026 market transition closed at USD 13.80 below the lower Bollinger band after a 6.25% five-session decline, without a configured volume anomaly.

daily_report_items: VALE full review: current Q2 filings support sound operating delivery and cash generation, but deterministic USD 9.00/USD 14.50/USD 20.00 scenarios produce only 1.09% expected return at USD 13.80 with material bear downside. Hold / Watch; the lower-Bollinger breach is timing risk, not a paper-trade signal.
